title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Comprehensive Guide
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary
-----
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended practices, reference architectures, and operational procedures for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-premises). It covers initial deployment prerequisites, recommended network and security configurations, on-prem packaging notes, day-2 operations (monitoring, scaling, backups), and detailed upgrade/rollback procedures. The intended audience is platform engineers, SREs, and customer success engineers responsible for private deployments.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: VPC-based private control plane + worker clusters, fully air-gapped on-prem packages, and hybrid modes where control plane is hosted and compute is customer-managed.
- Audience: SRE, Platform, Solutions Engineering, Customer Ops.
- Included: network diagrams (textual), config templates, deployment checklist, day-2 runbook, upgrade/rollback workflow, customer requirements library.

High-level reference architecture
--------------------------------
- Control plane options:
  - Customer-managed private control plane (recommended for regulated customers).
  - Redwood-hosted control plane with VPC peering/PrivateLink for customers requiring reduced ops.
- Compute plane:
  - Dedicated GPU nodes in customer VPC or on-prem cluster (NVIDIA A100, H100, or equivalent).
  - Multi-tenant pods isolated by Kubernetes namespaces and node pools, or VM-based workers for air-gapped installs.
- Network layout (VPC):
  - Management subnet (control-plane API, console)
  - Worker subnet(s) (GPU instances)
  - Storage subnet (object storage / NFS / S3-compatible endpoints)
  - Bastion / jump-host for maintenance

Prerequisites checklist
-----------------------
1. Account & access
   - AWS/Azure/GCP account with admin access for provisioning (or on-prem hardware ready).
   - Customer-provided KMS or HSM details for key management (if required).
2. Networking
   - CIDR allocation for control and worker subnets (no overlap with customer on-prem CIDRs if VPN/DirectConnect is used).
   - DNS entries and TLS certs for control plane endpoints (wildcard or SAN cert).
   - NAT/egress configuration for worker nodes if updates/telemetry are required.
3. Capacity planning
   - GPU SKU, cores, memory requirements per expected throughput and SLOs.
   - Minimum cluster: 3 control-plane nodes, 3 worker nodes for HA (adjust by workload).
4. Storage
   - S3-compatible object store access details or NFS mount points for model artifacts and KV caches.
5. Identity & Security
   - RBAC mapping, OIDC provider or SAML metadata, and service accounts for automation.

Network and security requirements
---------------------------------
- Firewall rules (VPC):
  - Control plane API: TCP 443 inbound from configured client ranges.
  - Worker nodes: allow inbound from control plane on ports 10250 (kubelet), 50051 (gRPC), and custom runtime ports as configured.
  - Storage endpoints: allow egress to object storage on HTTPS.
- VPN/PrivateLink:
  - Recommend PrivateLink for minimal exposure. If using VPN/DirectConnect, validate MTU and BGP settings.
- Encryption:
  - TLS 1.2+ for all control plane endpoints.
  - At-rest encryption for model artifacts and logs via customer KMS.
- Secrets management:
  - Use KMS-backed secrets (HashiCorp Vault, cloud-managed secrets) for DB credentials and service keys.

On-prem packaging notes
-----------------------
- Packaging formats supported: OVA/AMI for VM installs, K8s Helm charts for Kubernetes-based installs, and tarball-based air-gapped installers.
- Installer components:
  1. Bootstrap tool (offline bundle + installer binary)
  2. Container images (registry or tarballs)
  3. Configuration templates (YAML) and sample secrets manifest
- Air-gapped install steps (summary):
  1. Transfer offline bundle to air-gapped environment via secure media.
  2. Load container images into local registry and verify checksums.
  3. Apply Helm manifests with customer-specific values (network, storage, KMS).
  4. Run post-install validation scripts to verify node readiness, model cache connectivity, and runtime health.

Deployment procedure (VPC-hosted compute)
----------------------------------------
1. Prepare networking: create VPC, subnets, routing, and security groups.
2. Provision control-plane certificates and DNS records.
3. Deploy control plane (Helm chart): set replicas=3 for API servers, configure storage backend, configure KMS integration.
4. Provision worker node groups with GPU SKUs and attach IAM roles for storage access.
5. Deploy runtime services: model puller, inference runtime, batching proxy, metrics exporters.
6. Run end-to-end smoke tests: authentication, model load, sample inference, latency check.
7. Handover to customer ops with runbook and access grants.

Day-2 operations (runbook summary)
----------------------------------
Monitoring and observability:
- Metrics to monitor:
  - Per-model latency P50/P95/P99, request rates, token throughput.
  - GPU utilization, memory pressure, OOM events.
  - KV cache hit ratio, model load times.
- Dashboards:
  - Per-cluster overview, per-model heatmaps, SLO error budget burn-down.
- Alerts & thresholds (recommended):
  - GPU utilization > 90% sustained for 10m -> alert to capacity team.
  - P99 latency > SLO * 1.5 -> page on-call.
  - Model load failures > 5% of requests -> create incident.

Backups and recovery:
- Model artifacts: replicate to customer-managed S3 with lifecycle policies.
- Database/backing store: daily snapshots and point-in-time recovery where supported.
- Test restores quarterly from backups to a staging cluster.

Scaling and capacity changes:
1. Horizontal scaling: add worker node pools for additional model classes.
2. Vertical scaling: replace worker nodes with larger GPU SKUs during maintenance windows.
3. Autoscaling: recommended to drive by queue depth and tail latency metrics; configure cooldowns and max surge limits.

Incident response and triage
---------------------------
- When latency or errors spike:
  1. Validate control plane reachability and worker health.
  2. Check model cache hit rates and recent model loads.
  3. Look for noisy tenants / routes and apply temporary rate limits or route to fallback model.
  4. If capacity constrained, enable burst pool or failover to Redwood-hosted model with customer approval.

Upgrade and rollback procedures
-------------------------------
Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Run full integration tests in staging with representative traffic.
- Ensure backups and snapshots complete and are validated.
- Communicate maintenance window and expected impact.
- Confirm operator and on-call availability.

Canary/rolling upgrade steps (recommended):
1. Stage 0: Create canary node pool with new runtime version (1-2 nodes).
2. Stage 1: Deploy control-plane patch to canary replica set (1 replica), run smoke tests.
3. Stage 2: Gradually shift <5% of traffic to canary control-plane and monitor SLOs for 30m.
4. Stage 3: If stable, roll control plane across remaining replicas with rolling restart (maxUnavailable=1).
5. Stage 4: Upgrade worker node pools incrementally (drain, replace, validate) with parallelism limit set to preserve capacity.

Rollback steps (if canary fails):
1. Immediately redirect traffic back to previous version (DNS or load-balancer weights).
2. Recreate failing pods with previous image tag or restore from snapshots for stateful components.
3. Run post-rollback validation suite and open a triage ticket with logs and trace IDs.

Post-upgrade validation checklist:
- End-to-end sample inference success, latency within SLOs, and no elevated error budget burn.
- Model artifacts load correctly and cache warm-up times acceptable.
- Metrics collectors, tracing, and logging are intact.

Customer requirements library (summary table)
--------------------------------------------
| Requirement category | Typical ask / Example value | Notes |
|----------------------|-----------------------------|-------|
| Security             | Customer KMS / HSM, TLS 1.2+ | Provide integration steps and Helm value examples |
| Network              | PrivateLink or DirectConnect / VPN | MTU and BGP validation required for DirectConnect |
| Compliance           | SOC2, GDPR region controls | May require restricted data flow and audit logging |
| Capacity             | 10 A100 GPUs minimum for production initial commit | Provide cost/throughput modeling templates |
| Backup & DR          | RPO: 1h, RTO: 4h typical for models and metadata | Tests quarterly |
| Observability        | 30d metrics retention, 90d logs | Tiered retention available as add-on |

Templates and commands
----------------------
- Example Helm values snippet (networking and storage):
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Config
  values:
    controlPlane:
      replicas: 3
      tlsCertificate: /etc/ssl/redwood.pem
    storage:
      s3_endpoint: https://s3.example.com
    kms:
      provider: aws-kms
      key_id: arn:aws:kms:...
- Validation commands:
  - kubectl get nodes --selector=node-role.kubernetes.io=worker
  - curl -sS https://control-plane.example.com/healthz
  - /opt/redwood/bin/post_install_check --verify-models

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Service owner: eng-private-deployments team (on-call rotation: private-deployments-sre@redwood.ai).
- Escalation: contact Platform Eng lead (pager: Ethan Clarke) for P1 incidents.

Appendix: common troubleshooting notes
-------------------------------------
- Model load timeout errors: verify object store credentials and endpoint DNS resolution.
- High GPU memory pressure: examine batching config and KV cache size; consider increasing node count or using larger SKUs.
- Inability to reach control plane from worker nodes: validate security group rules, route tables, and DNS search domains.
